Hackathon 2026 · UC4 R&D data source unification

Maize breeding data, from cross to decision

The five synthetic UC4 files, read as one breeding lifecycle: which crop, which lines, where and when they were tested, what was done to the plots, what was measured, and how that should line up in time.

1 crop (maize)150 lines 72 trials6 sites2024 to 2026 synthetic, read-only
LifecycleGermplasm TrialsTreatmentsObservations LabEvidenceChronology checks Appendix

Crop mismatch. The hackathon briefs describe a vegetable-seed business, but every UC4 record is field maize. Confirm with the UC4 expert whether the demo should present it as maize or as a stand-in for a vegetable crop.

Key findings

  • One crop: maize. A single CROP_GUID, SYN-MZ line IDs, flint/dent kernels and trials described as maize performance trials.
  • Every line is measured on exactly one field trait (30 lines per trait), so no candidate can be compared on yield and disease together.
  • The record does not follow a breeding calendar. All 12 chronology checks fail somewhere: 52% of parent links point to a younger parent, and 330 field observations sit in trials still marked PLANNED.
  • 69 events are dated after the data was extracted (harvests, lab results, completed operations, observations), and 46 records were last changed before they were created or observed.
  • 'Treatments' are only routine field operations: planting, fertiliser, irrigation, inspection and harvest. There is no product, rate or factor column, and quantity units vary within each operation type.
  • Breeding stage does not predict the existing decision: the most advanced stage, S3, is discarded most often. 16 lines have no lab result.

Lifecycle

Germplasm and crossing

150 maize lines, made by selfing, doubled haploids (Dihap) or crosses, at generations F1 to DH. Each line carries a breeding stage (DEV, then S1 to S3) and an existing advancement decision. In this synthetic set the three attributes are unrelated.

Lifecycle

Field trials

72 trials across 6 sites, typed as yield, disease or quality trials, each testing 10 lines with 2 to 4 replications. Trials start in spring; their observations run through the season.

Lifecycle

Field treatments

The data records the operations applied to trial plots, not experimental treatments. Trial design and protocol exist only as opaque IDs (4 designs, 9 protocols), so what was compared against what cannot be read from the files.

Lifecycle

Field observations

Five traits are scored in the field: yield, grain moisture, plant height, disease severity and days to flowering. Trial type does not decide which trait is measured.

Lifecycle

Lab tests

Lab results attach to a line, not a trial, so a result cannot be tied to the season or site it describes. Trait names and units are missing.

Lifecycle

Evidence at decision time

What a breeder would have in hand when deciding: one field trait per line, lab results for most lines, and weak links between the two.

Validation

Chronology checks

Each rule encodes an order the breeding calendar implies: seed exists before it is sown, parents precede offspring, harvest follows planting. The record-keeping rules test the dates against the extract itself: nothing can have happened after the data was pulled (26 Sep 2026 12:00), and a record cannot be edited before it exists. In real data these would block aggregation until resolved. For the demo, the assistant should surface them as reasons for amber, not hide them.

Every date is well-formed, and fields derived from dates (trial start year and week, the year in each line ID) agree with them. The timestamps still look generated rather than recorded: harvest, lab, operation and trial dates all fall at midnight, and every line was created at 09:00.

Appendix

File inventory and categorical detail

Appendix

Can categorical values be quantile-binned?

Not directly. Quantiles need an order. Ordinal fields (stage, quality flag, replications, year, operation status) were mapped to their rank. Nominal fields (origin, generation, kernel type, pollination, intended use, status) were replaced by the mean grain yield of their lines, then cut. Only the 30 lines measured for yield contribute, so each category mean rests on 3 to 20 lines. With 2 to 5 levels, several quantile edges tie and the four bins collapse (tied). Use these bins descriptively; as model features they would leak the target.
